SELECT m.c0006 AS first_name, m.c0001 AS last_name FROM t0000 m JOIN t0005 a ON a.c0001=m.c0002 GROUP BY m.c0002 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.c0000)>7

WITH fall AS (SELECT c0003 id FROM t0006 WHERE date(c0002) BETWEEN '2019-09-01' AND '2019-11-30'),
cnt AS (SELECT f.id, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.c0001) FROM t0005 a WHERE a.c0000=f.id) n FROM fall f),
ws AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.c0001) n FROM t0005 a JOIN t0006 e ON a.c0000=e.c0003 WHERE e.c0006='Women''s Soccer'),
av AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(n),1) a FROM cnt)
SELECT ws.n AS women_soccer_attendees, av.a AS avg_fall_2019_attendees,
 CASE WHEN ws.n>av.a THEN 'more' WHEN ws.n<av.a THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM ws, av

SELECT j.c0000 AS department,
 COUNT(DISTINCT j.c0001) AS majors_offered,
 COUNT(DISTINCT m.c0003) AS majors_held,
 ROUND(1.0*COUNT(m.c0002)/COUNT(DISTINCT j.c0001),2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM t0007 j LEFT JOIN t0000 m ON m.c0003=j.c0001
WHERE j.c0000 IN (SELECT c0000 FROM t0007 WHERE c0003='College of Humanities and Social Sciences')
GROUP BY j.c0000
note: returned counts of majors offered/held; question could also mean name lists

LEFT JOIN t0007 j ON j.c0000=d.dept
LEFT JOIN t0000 m ON m.c0003=j.c0001 AND m.c0002 IN (SELECT c0001 FROM t0005)
LEFT JOIN t0004 i ON i.c0000=m.c0002 AND i.c0002='Dues'
GROUP BY d.dept
